text:
maya: getting alerts for high NAT port usage in us-west-2 — seeing connection failures on model-pull workers and a ton of TIME_WAITs in metrics. A few apps report 502/504 to downstream model registry.

jordan: saw the alert too. can you paste the flow logs / cloudwatch snippet?

maya: pasted the last 5m of VPC flow logs: 
```
src=10.12.4.23 dst=13.32.101.4 proto=6 action=ACCEPT packets=1 bytes=78 start=1932104500 end=1932104501
src=10.12.4.24 dst=13.32.101.4 proto=6 action=ACCEPT packets=1 bytes=78 start=1932104501 end=1932104501
...
```

sam: quick hypothesis — our L7 sidecar (envoy) on model-pull pods is creating a ton of outbound TCP connections that aren't being reused, so the NAT gateway pool is being exhausted. We've got a lot of concurrent workers doing parallel downloads.

eli: +1. igrep on envoy stats shows `cluster.upstream_cx_total` spikes and `http1x.codec_reuse` low. HTTP/1.1 keepalives aren't reusing connections.

jordan: what's the per-pod pattern? short-lived connections to many model-host fqdns? or long-lived but many destinations?

sam: many distinct destination IPs (cdn/model-buckets) + each worker does transient pulls with varying hostnames. NAT SNAT mapping is per (srcIP, srcPort, dstIP, dstPort, protocol) so high fanout kills ephemeral ports fast.

maya: current NAT stats from account metrics: NAT Gateway NAT port exhaustion alarm firing at 78% of per-EIP ephemeral allocation. We're running 2 NAT gateways in the AZ.

eli: remediation checklist we discussed:
- reduce outbound connection churn by enabling HTTP/2 or persistent keepalives in envoy
- put heavy download traffic through a dedicated egress proxy/pooler (centralized outbound pool) so fewer source IPs/ports used
- increase NAT capacity (add ENIs/eips or additional NAT gateways across AZs)
- patch pods to batch model pulls instead of parallel per-worker pulls with jitter

jordan: I'd add: consider switching to a NLB with preserving source IP for some traffic (if the destination supports it) or move pulls into s3 signed URLs through a VPC endpoint (reduces NAT).

maya: immediate blameless mitigation: throttled model-pull job concurrency via k8s job controller (reduction from 200 -> 40 concurrent pulls) and added jitter in rollout. Metrics show ephemeral port usage dropping after ~60s.

sam: we should also flip envoy to HTTP/2 upstream for the registry endpoints — that gives stream multiplexing and cuts connection count. I'll open a PR for envoy config: `use_http2: true`, set `max_connections` and `idle_timeout` to sane values.

eli: long-term: implement an egress-proxy service in each AZ (envoy/haproxy) that reuses connections and performs caching. That centralizes outbound sockets and preserves NAT ports. We'll need a small RFC.

jordan: logging & detection: created a dashboard showing ephemeral port saturation by subnet + top srcPod->dstIP tuples. Also added an alert when NAT port usage > 65% for 5m.

maya: ops-bot created ticket INF-4821 for infra changes (add NATs + egress-proxy RFC + envoy PR). For now we keep throttles in place.

ops-bot: Ticket INF-4821 created and assigned to eng-infra with priority P1. https://tickets.internal/INF-4821

sam: quick note — for testing, we reproduced the behavior locally by spinning 1000 short tcp clients from a single node to a few endpoints; `ss -s` showed TIME_WAITs piling up. Sample repro script attached in the PR.

eli: also checking kernel settings for TIME_WAIT reuse isn't applicable for nat-gateway (managed), but on bastion/nat-instance we could tune `tcp_tw_reuse` if we used nat instances. For NAT gateway we have to rely on better connection reuse or more NAT port capacity.

jordan: action items:
- sam: PR for envoy http2 + keepalive config (ETA 1d)
- maya: keep concurrency throttle + monitor (ETA now)
- eli: draft RFC for egress-proxy + costing (ETA 3d)
- infra: explore adding a 3rd NAT gateway in us-west-2a and 2b to spread load (ops ticket INF-4821)

maya: thanks — glue note: if anyone sees model-pull failures in the next hour, ping here and we'll escalate to immediate NAT add.

jordan: thanks, good catch. :thumbsup:
